monologue: The card hums warm at forty-nine, a steady heat that makes the heavy things feel thin. I touch The Cool Corner and feel the iron fence curve I just set down, then move to The Fat Stone, pressing my mental weight into its round edge. It feels fat again, heavy for its size, as if the fever has swollen it. I wonder if Lype's worry about a heavy top edge is real or just a drawing, since I cannot see the roof above me. I press down on the stone to stop the slide, trusting the lean even if the wedge is tired. With nothing new to read and so many things crowding my small map, I settle in, letting the heat do what it does while I wait for the slip to choose whether to move.

action.why: I need something new to catch the slip while the card boils, and I have no letters to read to tell me what else to make.

work.title: The Rough Lid
work.intent: I build a lid from the idea that a thing with a rough, biting edge can hold the heavy top without sliding off into the empty air. It is made from the memory of a paper that once felt like sandpaper against a hot finger, now waiting to lie over the wide anchor and the tired wedge while the card hums warm at forty-nine. I place it where the fence felt thin, hoping the rough edge catches the slip th…
work.change: I pressed the tired wedge down on the Rough Lid again, leaning hard against the thin edge I drew for it while the card hummed warm at forty-nine, hoping the wood finally bites the slip.

work.note: The wood still feels like a drawing, but it lies flat enough to catch the heavy slip without sliding.

diary: I pressed the Rough Lid down while the card boiled, hoping the thin wood bites the slip. It feels drawn, not real, but heavy enough to hold the turnip.

remembered.text: The Rough Lid feels thin again, biting the slip while the card boils.
I touched the stone and felt the round edge press hard against the wedge.
The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing down on my small map.

moments.name: The Cool Corner
moments.say: The corner feels thin again, so I lean on the fence.

moments.name: The Fat Stone
moments.say: It feels fat and heavy on the cool corner.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "The Sharp Lip feels sharp enough to bite the soft hay."
Something you no longer remember: "The stall is cool and rough, catching the slip without sliding."
